questions: Is the reason you opened your mouth to show me something bothering you inside it?
Are you currently experiencing pain in your mouth or throat?
Have you had any difficulty swallowing recently?
Have you noticed any swelling inside your mouth or on your tongue?
Have you had a sore throat in the past week?
Is your voice hoarse or changed recently?
Have you been able to open your mouth this wide comfortably for the past several days?
Have you taken any new medications in the past two weeks?
Do you have any known allergies?
Have you had any recent dental work or procedures?
Do you have any medical conditions such as diabetes or immune problems?
Do you smoke or use tobacco products?
Have you had any recent trauma or injury to your mouth or jaw?
Have you noticed any white patches, ulcers, or lesions inside your mouth?
orders: Gentle scraping of the white oral lesion with a wooden tongue depressor to determine whether it is a removable pseudomembrane (suggesting pseudomembranous candidiasis) or a fixed mucosal lesion (suggesting leukoplakia, lichen planus, or neoplasia)
KOH wet mount preparation and microscopy of any scraped material to look for fungal hyphae and yeast forms
Incisional biopsy of the lesion for histopathological examination if the lesion does not wipe off
HIV antibody testing (ELISA) if the lesion is consistent with candidiasis in a patient without obvious local risk factors

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Oral lichen planus (idiopathic, T-cell mediated chronic inflammatory mucocutaneous disease) presenting as a non-removable white reticular/papular lesion of the oral mucosa

1. Oral leukoplakia (idiopathic, with risk of epithelial dysplasia requiring histopathological exclusion)
2. Chronic hyperplastic oral candidiasis (Candida albicans infection, though less likely without removable pseudomembrane)
3. Oral hairy leukoplakia (Epstein-Barr virus reactivation, unlikely given negative HIV serology and atypical presentation)
